content: Grapefruit increases the levels of tofacitinib by interfering with the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient. No specific dose adjustment is recommended when tofacitinib is coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. However, reduce the dose of tofacitinib if coadministered with both moderate CYP3A4 and potent CYP2C19 inhibitors. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of trazodone by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of triazolam by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of vadadustat through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient. OAT1/OAT3 inhibitors may increase vadadustat AUC. Monitor closely for excessive or rapid increases in hemoglobin response and for adverse reactions. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of valbenazine by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the valbenazine dose to 40 mg once daily when coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of vamorolone by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the starting dose of vamorolone to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day if the patient weighs more than 50 kg. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of vardenafil by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient. Grapefruit increases the levels of vemurafenib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor the patient. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of verapamil by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of zuranolone by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the dose of zuranolone if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of alfentanil by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of abemaciclib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase plasma levels of abemaciclib and its metabolites. Patients should avoid grapefruit products. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of acalabrutinib with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., up to 7 days), temporarily interrupt treatment with acalabrutinib. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of adagrasib by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of adagrasib, a CYP3A4 substrate, with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors until adagrasib concentrations have reached steady-state (after ~8 days). If steady-state is not reached, concomitant use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors will increase adagrasib concentrations and the risk of its toxicities. Grapefruit increases the levels of afatinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Reduce the daily dose of afatinib by 10 mg if not tolerated when coadministered with P-gp inhibitors. Monitor closely. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of albendazole by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient.
